reasons: forecast_missing: the board registered questions to be answered BEFORE the line and the form carries no answer, or fewer answers than questions -- a forecast collected after the line is a rationalisation

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Bag of Tricks choosing the 3-Spark mode to place 3 Bombs dealing 5, then Kaboom! on Seapunk, then Firework Finale on Seapunk. This uses all 3 Energy and the available Spark economy: the 3-Spark Bag mode spends the starting 3 Sparks, the bombs detonating under Pounding Surprise restore 3 Sparks, and Firework Finale spends those 3 Sparks for 18 damage. The line prioritizes maximum damage and Spark cycling over block, since the enemy’s telegraphed 11 damage is survivable from 42 HP.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered Firework Finale first, then Kaboom!, then Duck and Cover or Spirited Away. That line would deal 25 damage and gain 5 or 12 Block, but it leaves the 3-Spark Bag mode unused and forgoes the bomb detonation Spark loop. I also considered Bag of Tricks in its 1-Bomb mode plus Firework Finale plus Kaboom!, but that is strictly worse damage and does not use the 3-Spark bomb mode.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The chosen line gives up all Block. If the enemy attacks for 11, I will end the turn at 31 HP instead of 37 or 42 HP under the block alternatives. It also exhausts Firework Finale, removing that card from the deck, and it commits the turn to a damage line that may still not kill Seapunk if the bombs only detonate once and no additional reaction damage occurs.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. If the enemy had telegraphed a much larger attack, a debuff, or a block-heavy intent, the no-block damage line would be less attractive. Against a higher attack, Spirited Away or Duck and Cover would become more important, and I might choose Firework Finale plus block instead of the full bomb-and-Firework damage line. Against a weaker attack or a non-attack intent, the chosen line remains the same.

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
